stem: In \(\triangle PQR\), point S is the midpoint of side QR. If PQ = 11, PR = 17, PS = 13, find QR.
In \(\triangle ABC\), AB = 10, AC = 7, BC = 9 then find the length of the median drawn from point C to side AB.

In the figure 2.28 seg PS is the median of \(\triangle PQR\) and PT \(\perp\) QR. Prove that,
(1) \(PR^2 = PS^2 + QR \times ST + \left(\frac{QR}{2}\right)^2\)
ii) \(PQ^2 = PS^2 - QR \times ST + \left(\frac{QR}{2}\right)^2\)
In \(\triangle ABC\), point M is the midpoint of side BC. If \(AB^2 + AC^2 = 290\) cm\(^2\), AM = 8 cm, find BC.

In figure 2.30, point T is in the interior of rectangle PQRS. Prove that, \(TS^2 + TQ^2 = TP^2 + TR^2\)
(As shown in the figure, draw seg AB \(\parallel\) side SR and A-T-B)
[Note: marked ★ (challenging) in the textbook.]
